glossary.definition: An unaged tequila class. In other spirits the same words can mean different classes or nothing legal at all; class terms are spirit-specific.

NOM-070-SCFI-2016 defines six mezcal classes: blanco o joven (no subsequent process), madurado en vidrio (over 12 months in glass), reposado (2–12 months in wood), añejo (over 12 months in wood containers under 1000 L), abocado con (ingredients added, e.g. worm, damiana, honey) and destilado con (distilled with ingredients, e.g. turkey or chicken breast — the pechuga tradition belongs here). Abocado and joven are different classes, not synonyms; the class list is separate from the three production categories (mezcal, artesanal, ancestral).

Wood-rested classes with spirit-specific rules. Tequila and mezcal reposado both begin at a two-month minimum, although their other requirements differ (mezcal reposado runs 2–12 months; mezcal añejo over 12 months in wood under 1000 L). Tequila rules still do not transfer to raicilla.
A mezcal made with fruit and/or a raw chicken or turkey breast suspended during a (usually third) distillation — a specific production tradition, not a spirit category of its own.

A batch made from multiple agave species, typically harvested and fermented together. An ensamble needs composition evidence; it is not simply a post-distillation blend, and it is not a separate spirit family.
An aged spirit filtered (often through charcoal) to remove colour while keeping some wood character. It is a finishing choice, not a legal class in most categories.

A NOM (Norma Oficial Mexicana) is an official Mexican standard; the NOM number printed on a tequila or mezcal label identifies the certified producer's registration under that standard. It is distinct from other label marks such as certification seals or holograms issued by a conformity-evaluation body. Absence of a NOM number (as with uncertified tuxca) means the producer is not registered under a denomination-of-origin scheme — not lower quality, and not exemption from other labelling requirements.
Regional words for a small distillery: vinata in Sonora, taberna in Jalisco raicilla country, palenque in Oaxaca. Same function, different tradition.
Small producers label batches; batch details (agave mix, ABV, maker) can differ materially between bottles of the same brand. Batch-specific facts must not silently become brand-wide facts.
A composition claim about fermentables, distinct from quality: agave-based traditions with disclosed non-agave fermentables (some comiteco) are included with their composition stated honestly.
